gen-luckiest-guy-gf-hammersmith-one: Loud, grinning, and a bit cheeky: Luckiest Guy hits hard with its poured-ink strokes and high mean line. And Hammersmith One does the quieter job, its rounded, cord-like strokes keeping text friendly and clean.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-inder: One length of bent tubing seems to shape every Luckiest Guy letter, cheerful and loud with a high, mean line. But Inder keeps the text low-key, with little height difference between its cases.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-jaldi: Luckiest Guy is all poured-ink cheer, with no swelling in its outlines. Jaldi follows in a brushed, tightly packed sans-serif, its tall lowercase and gaping c making a long stretch of text feel approachable and easy to settle into.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Luckiest Guy shouts cheerfully up top, its diagonals as thick as its uprights and its e opening clearly to the right. Kdam Thmor Pro, modern, with bowls that fill the line, takes over below.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-krona-one: Luckiest Guy brings stencil-cut letters of steady width and a mean high line, loud and cheerful from the first word. Krona One lets the text spread out, loosely spaced and sturdy.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-magra: Magra reads big-bodied and businesslike, every lowercase word feeling full and solid on the line. Luckiest Guy, drawn as if with one marker tip, adds the cheerful shout, so long text still feels lively.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-matemasie: Wide-open fun meets tidy restraint here. Luckiest Guy handles the shouting with its open, cheerful letters, while Matemasie, a plain sans with closed forms and broad gaps, handles the steady talking.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-mitr: Luckiest Guy is the cheerful loudmouth, every line looking drawn with one pen tip. Mitr then settles in with barely any gap between x-height and cap height, so a long passage feels compact and friendly.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-momo-trust-display: Loud, cheerful, and blunt-edged, Luckiest Guy has no tapering where its strokes meet. And Momo Trust Display, a sans-serif with drifting letters and a generous x-height, gives longer text room to breathe.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-mukta: Mukta reads tall-bodied and tidy, with small letters that stand up straight on the line. Luckiest Guy, cut like constant-width ribbon, is the cheerful loud one, while Mukta does the patient work.
